atlases.title: Egypt and the Ancient Near East
atlases.blurb: The first cities: temple towns on the Nile, brick metropolises between the Tigris and Euphrates, and the palace terraces of the Persian kings.

maps.title: Thebes
maps.subtitle: Temples of Karnak and Luxor, 1250 BCE
maps.blurb: The religious capital of New Kingdom Egypt, its east bank given over to the great temples of Amun.

maps.title: Babylon
maps.subtitle: Nebuchadnezzar's city, 575 BCE
maps.blurb: A walled city on the Euphrates with the Ishtar Gate, the processional way and the ziggurat Etemenanki.

maps.title: Persepolis
maps.subtitle: Terrace of the Achaemenid kings, 500 BCE
maps.blurb: Ceremonial capital of Darius and Xerxes, built on a stone terrace at the foot of the Mountain of Mercy.

atlases.title: The Classical Mediterranean
atlases.region: Greece, Rome and the Mediterranean shores
atlases.blurb: City-states and an empire around one sea: Greek agoras and theatres, then Rome's forums, baths and aqueducts from Britain to Egypt.

maps.title: Rome
maps.subtitle: Caput mundi, 100 CE
maps.blurb: The capital of the empire at its height: the Colosseum new, Trajan's Forum rising, a million people in the insulae.

maps.title: Athens
maps.subtitle: The city of Pericles, 430 BCE
maps.blurb: The Parthenon newly finished on the Acropolis, the Agora below, the Long Walls running to the Piraeus.

maps.title: Alexandria
maps.subtitle: Ptolemaic capital, 200 BCE
maps.blurb: Alexander's city on the Egyptian coast, with the Pharos lighthouse, the royal quarter and the Museum and Library.

maps.title: Carthage
maps.subtitle: The Punic city, 150 BCE
maps.blurb: Rome's great rival in its last years: the circular naval harbour, the Byrsa hill and the city walls.

atlases.title: Ancient India
atlases.blurb: From the planned brick cities of the Indus to the capitals of the Mauryan and Gupta kings on the Ganges plain.

maps.title: Mohenjo-daro
maps.subtitle: Indus city, 2500 BCE
maps.blurb: A grid of baked-brick houses with covered drains, a citadel mound and the Great Bath.

maps.title: Pataliputra
maps.subtitle: Mauryan capital, 300 BCE
maps.blurb: The capital of Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka on the Ganges, described by the Greek envoy Megasthenes.

maps.title: Taxila
maps.subtitle: Gateway city, 300 BCE
maps.blurb: A crossroads city of the north-west, known for its centre of learning and for the meeting of Indian and Greek worlds.

atlases.title: The Silk Road
atlases.region: Central Asia, from Persia to China
atlases.blurb: Oasis cities strung across deserts and mountains, where caravans traded silk, horses, paper and ideas between China, India, Persia and the West.

maps.title: Samarkand
maps.subtitle: Timur's capital, 1400
maps.blurb: Timur's showpiece city, with the Bibi-Khanym mosque and the Registan square of markets.

maps.title: Merv
maps.subtitle: Seljuk metropolis, 1100
maps.blurb: One of the largest cities of its age, an oasis capital ringed by walls, later destroyed by the Mongols.

maps.title: Dunhuang
maps.subtitle: Oasis of the caves, 800
maps.blurb: The last stop before the deserts of the Tarim, and the Buddhist cave temples of Mogao carved into the cliffs nearby.

atlases.title: Imperial China
atlases.region: The Yellow River and the north China plain
atlases.blurb: Capitals laid out on a grid around the emperor's palace: wards and markets, canals for grain, and walls with great gates.

maps.title: Chang'an
maps.subtitle: Tang capital, 750
maps.blurb: The largest city of its time, a vast walled grid of residential wards with the East and West Markets.

maps.title: Kaifeng
maps.subtitle: Northern Song capital, 1120
maps.blurb: A busy commercial city on the canals, the world of the scroll 'Along the River During the Qingming Festival'.

maps.title: Khanbaliq
maps.subtitle: Yuan capital, 1290
maps.blurb: Kublai Khan's new capital on the site of later Beijing, as Marco Polo described it.

atlases.title: The Islamic Golden Age
atlases.blurb: Caliphal capitals of scholars, mosques and markets, linked by pilgrimage and trade from Spain to Iraq.

maps.title: Baghdad
maps.subtitle: The Round City, 800
maps.blurb: Al-Mansur's circular capital on the Tigris, with the caliph's palace and great mosque at its centre.

maps.title: Córdoba
maps.subtitle: Umayyad capital, 950
maps.blurb: The largest city of western Europe in its day, with its Great Mosque and the palace-city of Madinat al-Zahra.

maps.title: Cairo
maps.subtitle: Fatimid city, 1050
maps.blurb: The walled royal city of the Fatimids, with the mosque of al-Azhar and its gates of Bab Zuwayla and Bab al-Futuh.

atlases.title: Medieval Europe
atlases.blurb: Walled towns of towers and churches, pilgrims and guilds, cathedrals rising over crowded streets and markets.

maps.title: Rome
maps.subtitle: City of pilgrims, 1300
maps.blurb: The first Jubilee year: baronial towers in the ruins, pilgrims crowding to St Peter's and the Lateran.

maps.title: Constantinople
maps.subtitle: Queen of cities, 1150
maps.blurb: The Byzantine capital behind its land walls, with Hagia Sophia, the Hippodrome and the harbours of the Golden Horn.

maps.title: Paris
maps.subtitle: Gothic Paris, 1250
maps.blurb: Notre-Dame and the Sainte-Chapelle on the Île de la Cité, the university on the Left Bank, the merchants on the Right.

maps.title: Venice
maps.subtitle: The lagoon republic, 1400
maps.blurb: A trading empire on islands: St Mark's, the Doge's Palace, the Arsenal and the Rialto market.

atlases.title: Renaissance Europe
atlases.region: Italy, Iberia and the Low Countries
atlases.blurb: New palaces, piazzas and domes, printing presses and banks, and ports facing an ocean world.

maps.title: Rome
maps.subtitle: Papal Rome, 1560
maps.blurb: Michelangelo's St Peter's rising, new straight streets cut by the popes, palazzi in the old Campus Martius.

maps.title: Florence
maps.subtitle: The Medici city, 1490
maps.blurb: Brunelleschi's dome over the cathedral, the Medici palace and the workshops of painters and goldsmiths.

maps.title: Lisbon
maps.subtitle: Port of the Indies, 1550
maps.blurb: The riverside capital of a sea empire, its palace on the Tagus waterfront and ships leaving for India and Brazil.

atlases.title: Mughal India
atlases.blurb: Red sandstone forts, white marble tombs and garden cities of the Mughal emperors.

maps.title: Delhi
maps.subtitle: Shahjahanabad, 1660
maps.blurb: Shah Jahan's new capital: the Red Fort on the Yamuna, the Jama Masjid and the bazaar of Chandni Chowk.

maps.title: Agra
maps.subtitle: City of the Taj, 1650
maps.blurb: The Agra Fort and the newly finished Taj Mahal, with riverside gardens along the Yamuna.

maps.title: Fatehpur Sikri
maps.subtitle: Akbar's city, 1585
maps.blurb: Akbar's red sandstone capital on a ridge, with the Buland Darwaza and the court of the Diwan-i-Khas.

atlases.title: Japan, from Nara to Edo
atlases.blurb: Capitals modelled on Chang'an, then castle towns and the great shogun's city of Edo.

maps.title: Nara
maps.subtitle: Heijō-kyō, 750
maps.blurb: A gridded capital on the Chinese model, with the great bronze Buddha of Tōdai-ji.

maps.title: Kyoto
maps.subtitle: Heian-kyō, 1000
maps.blurb: The court city of the Tale of Genji, its avenues laid out between the hills.

maps.title: Edo
maps.subtitle: The shogun's city, 1800
maps.blurb: One of the largest cities in the world, around the shogun's castle, with merchant quarters and the Nihonbashi bridge.

atlases.title: African Kingdoms
atlases.region: The Horn, the Sahel and the Zimbabwe plateau
atlases.blurb: Capitals of trade in gold, salt and ivory: stelae fields, mud-brick mosques and great stone enclosures.

maps.title: Aksum
maps.subtitle: City of the stelae, 350
maps.blurb: Capital of a trading kingdom of the Horn of Africa, with its tall carved stone stelae.

maps.title: Timbuktu
maps.subtitle: City of scholars, 1450
maps.blurb: A Saharan trading town with the mud-brick mosques of Djinguereber and Sankoré and their scholars.

maps.title: Great Zimbabwe
maps.subtitle: The stone city, 1350
maps.blurb: Dry-stone enclosures on the Zimbabwe plateau, the centre of a kingdom trading gold to the Indian Ocean coast.

atlases.title: Mesoamerica and the Andes
atlases.region: The Valley of Mexico to the Andes
atlases.blurb: Pyramid cities, island capitals on a lake and an empire of roads across the mountains.

maps.title: Teotihuacan
maps.subtitle: City of the gods, 450
maps.blurb: A great planned city along the Avenue of the Dead, with the Pyramids of the Sun and the Moon.

maps.title: Tenochtitlan
maps.subtitle: The island capital, 1519
maps.blurb: The Mexica capital on Lake Texcoco, joined to the shore by causeways, with the Templo Mayor at its heart.

maps.title: Cusco
maps.subtitle: Navel of the Inca world, 1530
maps.blurb: The Inca capital of fitted stone walls, the Coricancha temple and roads leading to every corner of the empire.
